regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; the texture is more interesting. IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirm the investment cycle is real — not budgeted. But core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) and commercial vehicle sales falling for two consecutive months to 12.6% YoY suggest goods movement is softening beneath the surface. The PMI composite at 55.9 is services-led — manufacturing at 55.1 is solid but not exceptional. Growth is genuine; its distribution is narrower than the headline implies.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 10-year high — is the number that should be keeping the MPC awake. Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY has already overshot the RBI's own revised forecast of 5.1% YoY, and food at 7.74% YoY is accelerating for the second consecutive month. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is the one comfort — but Brent at $112/bbl means the fuel component will not self-correct. The inversion: the RBI is forecasting inflation it has already missed, and the gap between its model and the data is widening, not closing.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth of 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence — keeps the CD ratio at 81%, the 73rd percentile historically. Services credit at 24.3% YoY is the highest in the dataset; NBFC credit at 15.8% YoY is rising for the second consecutive month. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% during a rate-pause cycle, the eventual correction came via macro-prudential tightening on risk weights, not rate hikes. The incentive structure for banks — grow credit for fee income, worry about deposits later — has not changed. The regulator's patience has a limit.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being eroded in real time: CPI at 5.54% YoY means the ex-ante real rate is effectively zero. The RBI's extended pause made sense when inflation was at 4.83% YoY; it is harder to defend at 5.54% YoY with fuel at a 10-year high. The second-order effect: a zero real rate with credit growing at 19.4% YoY is a deposit-mobilisation problem waiting to become a systemic one. The RBI is not behind the curve on growth — it is behind the curve on inflation, and the two are now pulling in opposite directions.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1%) and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) are the two numbers that validate the investment cycle. At 77.4%, utilisation is in the zone — historically, private capex accelerates meaningfully above 75% — so the pipeline is credible. Credit to industry at 18.2% YoY and agriculture at 17.2% YoY, both rising for two consecutive months, confirm the broadening. The risk: core sector at 4.8% YoY is the physical output check on the financial flows — and it is decelerating. Watch for the gap between credit-funded capex and actual output to widen.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is solid but not accelerating — up from ₹1,99,853 cr / month, with the prior month at ₹2,00,640 cr / month. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are falling for the second consecutive month (from 26.1% to 16.0% to 7.9%) — a sharp deceleration that the GST headline obscures. Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are the informal economy's signal: rural demand is alive. The divergence — mass-market two-wheelers strong, premium passenger vehicles fading — is the classic pattern when urban discretionary softens while rural incomes recover. GST's formalization effect is doing part of the work; genuine demand growth is doing less.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1% → 19.4% credit; 9.9% → 17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 57th percentile. Services sector credit surging at 24.3% YoY, highest in dataset.","implication":"RBI will face pressure to tighten liquidity or signal rate cuts are off the table longer than markets expect. Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they'll face margin compression as deposit costs rise. Watch for RBI to deploy CRR cuts or OMOs within 4-6 weeks if credit-deposit gap widens further.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level; historically, ratios above 85% preceded NBFC stress (2018-19). Current divergence is driven by services and vehicle credit, not distressed lending.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (latest), rising 3 consecutive months (₹29,845 → ₹31,961 → ₹32,297 → ₹32,490), now at 93rd percentile. BUT: SIP YoY growth at 10.7% (down from 15% → 19.85% → 14%), signalling deceleration in account growth.","implication":"SIP inflows are hitting records, but average ticket size is rising faster than account growth — affluent retail is entering, not mass-market expansion. DIIs at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) are offsetting FII outflows (₹-49,935 cr / month, 17th percentile), so domestic support is structural. Watch for SIP account growth to stabilise; if it falls below 5% YoY, retail saturation is real.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile are at all-time highs; historically, such peaks preceded 8-12% market corrections (2021, 2022) as retail chased momentum.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort Zone","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% YoY, now at 95th percentile — the highest in the dataset. CPI headline at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83%), food inflation at 7.74% YoY (up from 5.97%), both rising 2 consecutive months. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) and defensive FMCG; underweight rate-sensitive sectors (auto, real estate). Hedge INR weakness — fuel inflation typically weakens the rupee as import bills rise. Monitor FAO food index at 136 (61st percentile); if it breaks above 140, food inflation will persist into Q3.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is the highest since 2022; historically, such spikes preceded 6-month periods of RBI hawkishness and INR weakness.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surge Masks GCC Consolidation, Not IT Expansion","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), up from 11.2 mn sq ft / quarter, but flagged as strong-negative signal (score: -86, 7th percentile). Recent trend: 24.6 → 2.6 → 19.5 → 14.1 → 15.08 → 14.1 (volatile, not sustained). Office vacancy at 14.8% vacant (up from 14.5%), at 43rd percentile. Nifty IT index is flat (not in dataset, but implied by Nifty50 at 23,053, 74th percentile). CONTRAST: Nikkei225 at 63,290 (100th percentile, rising 3 of last 5), Euro Stoxx50 at 6,131 (100th percentile, rising 4 of last 5). Global PMI composite at 54.3 (84th percentile, rising 2 in a row). US PMI at 58.4 (91st percentile). India PMI at 55.9 (85th percentile).","implication":"Office absorption is rising, but NOT because IT services are expanding — it's Global Capability Centers (GCCs) from tech giants (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Apple) consolidating operations in Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune. Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shedding headcount. This means: (1) Commercial real estate is decoupling from IT services stocks — don't use office absorption as a proxy for IT sector health. (2) GCCs are higher-margin, lower-headcount operations — they won't drive employment or wage growth. (3) Nifty IT will underperform despite office demand. Underweight IT services; overweight commercial real estate REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) and logistics/data centre plays. The 'office recovery' narrative is a trap — it's a GCC consolidation, not an IT boom.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 7th percentile is historically weak, yet rising — this inversion signals structural change (GCC consolidation) rather than cyclical recovery. Historically, sustained office absorption above 15 mn sq ft / quarter preceded IT services wage inflation and hiring booms (2015-2018); current data shows neither.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Investment Cycle Accelerates — Consumption Quietly Decelerates

The facts:

  • IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirm the investment upcycle is in the sweet spot for private capex acceleration.
  • GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is stable, but passenger vehicle sales have decelerated sharply — 26.1% → 16.0% → 7.9% YoY over three months.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural demand is holding; the urban-rural divergence is widening, not narrowing.
  • But core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) is the physical output check — goods movement is softening while financial flows accelerate.
  • PMI composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) is services-led; manufacturing at 55.1 is solid but not the driver.

The tension: Capex indicators and PMI point to expansion; the consumption decomposition — PV sales halving in three months while two-wheelers surge — signals a bifurcation between urban discretionary and rural mass-market demand that the headline GDP cannot resolve.

Bottom line: Watch PV sales for a third consecutive monthly deceleration — if it prints below 5% YoY, urban consumption is the story, not the investment cycle.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Re-Acceleration Meets Synchronised Central Bank Tightening

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR at 3.4% SAAR (rising three consecutive quarters) and US PMI composite at 58.4 (91st percentile) signal genuine re-acceleration — not a survey artefact.
  • But US CPI at 3.72% YoY is rising for the third consecutive month, and US 10Y Treasury at 4.98% yield (90th percentile) means real tightening is already embedded.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. — a 10-year high, rising for the second consecutive month — is the underappreciated tail: yen carry unwinds hit EM liquidity with a 60–90 day lag.
  • ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (rising two in a row); Euro Stoxx 50 at a 10-year-high 100th percentile — equity markets are pricing growth, bond markets are pricing tightening.
  • China GDP at 4.4% YoY with PMI composite recovering to 52.1 — a floor, not a rebound; commodity reflation from China is not the story this cycle.

The tension: DM growth surveys are at multi-year highs, but three central banks are tightening simultaneously and US inflation is re-accelerating — the equity rally is pricing the growth signal while ignoring the rate signal.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the single most underpriced risk for India FII flows; watch the next BOJ meeting for a move above 1.5% p.a.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows Hold the Line — FII Exit Masks Structural Fragility

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising for three consecutive months — retail is on autopilot and providing a structural bid.
  • DII equity net inflows at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) are absorbing FII equity net outflows of ₹-49,935 cr / month (17th percentile, worst in dataset) almost exactly.
  • But SIP YoY growth at 10.7% YoY is decelerating sharply — down from 19.85% — signalling the account-addition engine is slowing even as the per-account ticket rises.
  • MF AUM at ₹82.64 lakh cr is down from ₹87.08 lakh cr; NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) confirm institutional conviction is not following retail.
  • Gold in INR at ₹11,895/g (99th percentile) — the market is hedging INR weakness even as the spot rate at 95.24 ₹/USD appears stable.

The tension: The DII-FII offset is arithmetically clean but structurally fragile: DII absorption depends on SIP continuity, and SIP account growth is decelerating precisely as FII outflows are at a dataset worst.

Bottom line: If SIP YoY growth falls below 8% YoY, the DII absorption buffer thins — watch next month's SIP account addition data as the leading indicator.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand Holds Premium; Equities Price Growth the Data Doesn't Guarantee

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 2 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $144.8 bn (16.2% YoY) are the funding source.
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum — sales 15% YoY, launches 120% YoY, only 28 months of unsold inventory — but the launch-to-sales ratio flags oversupply risk within 6 quarters.
  • Home loan disbursements at ₹94,000 cr / quarter (2nd percentile, 10-year low) at an average rate of 8.1% p.a. — affordability is the binding constraint, not demand intent.
  • Nifty 50 at 23,053 (74th percentile) with India VIX at 15.3 (10th percentile) — the market is pricing calm; FII outflows of ₹-49,935 cr / month suggest the calm is borrowed.
  • But REIT unit prices — Embassy at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — are down 10–28% from prior prints, pricing office stress the absorption headline obscures.

The tension: Equity markets are at the 74th percentile with VIX at the 10th — pricing a benign outcome — while REITs, FII flows, and home loan disbursements are all at multi-year lows, pricing stress.

Bottom line: Avoid REITs until office vacancy stabilises below 13% vacant; in equities, hedge the FII outflow tail with Nifty puts if the index approaches 23,500.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Inflation, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $112/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill; CPI is already above the RBI's own forecast.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — yen carry unwind historically hits EM FII flows within 60–90 days; FII outflows are already at ₹-49,935 cr / month, the dataset worst.
  • CD ratio at 81% (73rd percentile) with credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — if deposit growth slips back toward 10% YoY, NBFC funding costs reprice sharply.
  • PV sales decelerating to 7.9% YoY (from 26.1% three months ago) — if this extends to a third consecutive month below 10% YoY, urban consumption is in contraction, not moderation.

The tension: All three risks — inflation overshoot, carry unwind, and credit-deposit divergence — are individually manageable; the tail risk is that a BOJ move triggers FII outflows that tighten domestic liquidity precisely when the RBI cannot cut rates because CPI is above target.

Bottom line: Watch November CPI: a print above 5.8% YoY forces the RBI's hand and removes the last argument for a rate pause into FY27.

"}
